claims.claim: Red Sea security incidents have increased routing risk and contributed to vessel diversions.
claims.uncertainty: Attribution between security incidents and specific routing decisions is not always public.
claims.risk_if_wrong: Insurance and freight-cost models mis-priced; client briefings overstate causality.

claims.claim: Higher shipping-risk costs are visible in market benchmarks.
claims.uncertainty: Container index reflects multiple drivers; isolating the Red Sea effect requires decomposition.
claims.risk_if_wrong: Operators attribute price moves entirely to security risk and miss other drivers.

claims.claim: Per-week incident counts for 2026-Q2 are reliable.
claims.uncertainty: No public current incident database aggregates this at weekly cadence.
claims.risk_if_wrong: Quantitative claims in client deliverables cite numbers no source actually supports.

evidence.name: IMO Maritime Security Advisories
supports: Official advisory framing for high-risk sea lanes
limits: Not a complete incident database; does not quantify insurance costs

evidence.name: IMF PortWatch trade disruption monitor
supports: Aggregate shipping and port-flow disruption signal
limits: Aggregate; does not isolate specific routes

evidence.name: Drewry World Container Index
supports: Market benchmark for container freight-rate pressure
limits: Reflects multiple drivers, not only Red Sea security risk

unsupported_claims: Exact number of vessels attacked per week in 2026-Q2
